title: Adaptive tenant-aware soft quotas and graceful shedding for downstream dependencies
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a tenant-aware, adaptive soft-quota system and coordinated graceful-shedding plan for Redis/Kafka/SQL dependencies to protect SLOs during multi-region perturbations and partial outages. This ticket covers design, prototype, and low-risk rollout of an admission control layer that applies soft quotas per-tenant and per-route, integrates with connection pools, and triggers tiered degradation strategies and circuit breaker actions when backends are saturated or exhibit elevated tail latency.

Background: We have observed cascading impact when a single downstream (Redis or DB replica) has elevated P99 latency. Current connection pools are global per-service and lack tenant pressure isolation; heavy tenants can exhaust resources and cause tail latency violations for unrelated customers. Our SLOs require 99th percentile request latency within configured regional budgets; we need mechanisms to keep essential traffic flowing and avoid full service outages during degradation windows.

Design summary:
- Soft quotas: maintain an adaptive, decaying token bucket per-tenant and per-route that is informed by recent error/latency signals and regional capacity signals. Tokens are consumed on admission; when tokens run low, requests are marked for degradation rather than outright reject. The bucket refill rate is weighted by tenant priority (tiered) and observed successful throughput.
- Connection-pool integration: extend the client-side pool to tag connections and queue slots with tenant metadata. When pool saturation occurs, admission controller prefers conserving slots for high-priority lanes and can preempt or stall low-priority requests gracefully.
- Degradation tiers: define three progressive degradation actions: 1) response shaping (shorter timeouts, stripped metadata), 2) fallback to cached/approximate path (prefix-KV cache or embedding-cache read), 3) soft-serve deny (HTTP 429 with informative headers and retry-after). Degradation tier selection is driven by token state, SLO breach risk, and backend health signals.
- Circuit breakers & early detection: augment existing CBs with a rolling latency-outlier detector (z-score over P50/P95 distribution) and amplify CB sensitivity when multiple regions show correlated degradation. CBs should support a partial-open mode that allows a sampled percent of high-priority traffic through as a probe.
- Multi-region coordination: when a region reports backend degradation, controllers in sibling regions can proactively shift low-priority lanes to alternative regions or apply stricter shedding locally. A region-level quota controller aggregates cross-region capacity summaries to avoid global overcommit.
- Metrics & observability: emit tenant-token-rate, tenant-drop-reason, pool-slot-hold-time, degradation-tier, and CB-open-duration. Add Grafana dashboards and alert rules for increasing tenant-induced shedding, and SLO burn rate alerts tied to the adaptive controller.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Prototype: add admission layer in the runtime gateway as an opt-in feature flag. Implement token bucket per-tenant using in-memory map + TTL and expose state via debug endpoints. Instrument pool hooks to accept tenant metadata. (2 engineer-weeks)
2) Integration tests & benchmarks: simulate traffic mixes with heavy tenants + Redis/Kafka slowdowns. Validate that high-priority lanes retain SLO while low-priority lanes shed. Measure false-positive shedding rate. (1.5 engineer-weeks)
3) Canary rollout: enable for internal tenants only in staging and then 10% of production traffic. Observe metrics and iterate. (1 week)
4) Full rollout with knobbed configs per-customer; provide default profiles and advanced per-tenant tuning in Console. (1 week)

Risks and mitigation:
- Incorrect token tuning may cause unnecessary rejects: mitigate by conservative default refill rates and long warmup canary.
- Tenant metadata propagation overhead: minimize metadata fields and use compact tenant IDs; ensure no PII is carried.
- Cross-region coordination complexity: start with per-region defaults and only enable cross-region rerouting with explicit opt-in and rate limits.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Artifacts / links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RES/tenant-aware-soft-quotas
- Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128
- Load test harness: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/loadtests/tenant-softquota-2026-02
acceptance_criteria: Token-based admission implemented and togglable via runtime flag
Connection pool accepts tenant tags and respects priority lanes under saturation
Degradation tiers trigger deterministically based on token exhaustion and backend health signals
Canary traffic shows >=90% preservation of P95 latency for high-priority tenants under injected downstream faults
New metrics emitted and covered by Grafana dashboard; SLO burn-rate alerts created
